title: Is Traveling for Rehab Good?
metaDescription: Finding the best rehab for you is a crucial step in recovery. Learn more about the benefits of traveling for rehab and how to get help today

blocks.text: December 28, 2021

There are many options when it comes to getting help for an addiction. You can choose an inpatient or outpatient program. If you go the inpatient route, you can opt for a facility close to home, or you may decide to travel to another city or state to get the care you need.
Traveling for rehab has its share of advantages and disadvantages. This article will review what’s involved so you can make the decision that’s right for you.
Signs of Drug or Alcohol Addiction
The first step will be determining whether you or a loved one needs to get help. Here are some signs of drug and alcohol addiction to be aware of.
Increased Tolerance: The first thing you will notice is an increased tolerance to the drug you are taking. You will need to take more of the drug to get the same effects.

Withdrawal Symptoms: After taking drugs for a while, your body will get used to having them in its system, and it will be unable to function normally without them. It will begin producing withdrawal symptoms when it’s clean. The only short-term way of getting rid of these symptoms is to take more of the drug.
Other signs of drug and alcohol addiction will vary depending on the drug being used, but here are some common symptoms:
Mood swings
Troubled relationships
Legal issues
Financial issues
Deceptive behavior
Spending a lot of time trying to obtain and do the drug
Changes in appetite
Changes in sleep habits
Is Traveling for Rehab a Good Idea?
Part of determining if traveling for rehab is a good idea is deciding if you require inpatient or outpatient treatment. Inpatient treatment is recommended if:
You can spend time enough time away from work or home for long-term recovery. Inpatient treatment is typically 30, 60, or 90 days.
You have an unhealthy home life due to an abusive or druggie environment.
Your addiction is severe, and you require 24/7 supervision to ensure your treatment is updated, and relapse doesn’t occur.
You can afford an inpatient program.
If you think that an inpatient program is right for you, you must further consider if you are better off traveling for rehab or going to a facility close to home.
Traveling for rehab is recommended because:
It will provide you with a new perspective.
It will remove you from stressful situations and people and places that drew you to using.
It will allow you to reflect on your old ways and make a change for the better.
It reduces the chances that you will leave rehab and go home.
Traveling for rehab also has its downsides including:
It’s an added expense. Patients will need to cover the cost of treatment and flights.
It keeps you far away from loved ones who may play an active role in your recovery.
It requires a bigger adjustment to society when you get back home.
The facility may not provide aftercare resources in your community.
How to Find the Best Rehab for Me

The type of rehab you choose will depend on your personal situation and what you feel is right for you. In addition to thinking about whether you want inpatient and outpatient and traveling for rehab, you should also consider the facility’s atmosphere, the types of treatment offered, the staff qualifications, and other features that are important to you.
